settings.name_in_paper: Conservative stochastic linear bandit with stage-wise constraints (known baseline reward)
unmapped: Stage-wise constraint <x_t,theta*> >= (1-alpha) r_{b_t} relative to a baseline action x_{b_t} given each round
The learner knows the conservatism level alpha, the baseline rewards r_{b_t}, and bounds r_l, r_h, kappa_l on baseline reward and baseline suboptimality gap (Assumption 4)
Action set contains the unit ball and <x,theta*> <= 1 for all x
Learner can play randomized conservative actions (1-rho) x_b + rho zeta_t with zeta_t of unit norm and covariance min eigenvalue sigma_zeta^2

settings.name_in_paper: Additional side constraint with bandit feedback
unmapped: Stage-wise constraint <x_t, mu*> >= (1-alpha) q_{b_t} with a separate unknown parameter mu*, observed through additional noisy bandit feedback w_t
The learner knows alpha, q_{b_t}, and bounds q_l, q_h, nu_l on the baseline constraint value and gap
Action set contains the unit ball
settings.definition_quote: we assume the constraint of the form <x_t, mu*> >= (1-alpha) q_{b_t} ... We assume that with playing an action x_t, the learner observes the following bandit feedback: w_t = <x_t, mu*> + chi_t

unmapped: Stage-wise constraint <x_t,theta*> >= (1-alpha) r_{b_t} with baseline rewards r_{b_t} unknown to the learner
The learner knows alpha, r_l and kappa_l
Action set contains the unit ball and <x,theta*> <= 1
settings.definition_quote: we consider the case where the expected reward of the action chosen by baseline policy, i.e., r_{b_t} is unknown to the learner. However, we assume that the learner knows the value of r_l

settings.name_in_paper: Safe linear bandit with constraint x^T B theta* <= C (Safe-LUCB setting of Amani et al.)
unmapped: Linear safety constraint x^T B theta* <= C with known matrix B and constant C > 0, no feedback on constraint value
Decision set convex compact containing the origin
The learner knows B, C and the safety gap Delta = C - x*^T B theta* > 0 (used in the algorithm's threshold)
settings.definition_quote: The learning environment is subject to the linear safety constraint x^T B theta* <= C, which needs to be satisfied at all rounds t with high probability ... the matrix B and the positive constant C are known to the learner.

source.label: thm:bounding_term_I_regret_of_safe_lts
source.quote: Let $\lambda , L \geq 1$. On event $\{ \theta_\star \in \mathcal{E}_t, \forall t \in [T] \}$, and under  Assumption \ref{ass:lowerbound_reward}, we can bound Term I in \eqref{regret:decompos} as: Term I \leq ( \beta_T(\delta') + \gamma_T(\delta') (1+\frac{4}{p}) ) \sqrt{2 T d \log{ (1 + \frac{T L^2}{\lambda})}}  + \frac{4 \gamma_T(\delta')}{p} \sqrt{\frac{8T L^2}{\lambda} \log{\frac{4}{\delta}}}

results.notes: Bounds only Term I of the regret decomposition (rounds where non-conservative actions are played); total regret = Term I + |N_T^c|(kappa_h + rho_1(r_h+S)). Order O(d^{3/2} sqrt(log d) sqrt(T) log^{3/2} T). The constant C in gamma is unexplained in the paper. Also stated to apply to SCLTS-BF and SCLTS2.
